1. Review Inputs  
   In this iteration we are looking at the module decomposition to support use cases mainly UC-1, UC-2 and UC-7, as well support related quality attributes, concerns and constraints.

2. Establish Iteration Goal  
   The main goal of this iteration is to take foundational architectural patterns and further decompose the architecture into distinct modules, allocating their responsibilities across layers

3. Choose Elements to Refine  
   The elements to be refined are the prioritized use cases and the architecture layers

4. Choose Design Concepts that Satisfy Selected Drivers  
   The system architecture will continue to apply the facade pattern that maintains unified access for users, ensuring subsystems are encapsulated  
   A design concept being adopted in this iteration is layered architecture for explicit interface separation enabling independent evolution of modules

5. Instantiate Architectural Elements, Allocate Responsibilities and Define Interfaces  
   

| Element | Responsibility |
| :---- | :---- |
| User and user permission services | Manages user roles, access levels and system authorization |
| User authentication service | Authenticates users before allowing access to personal data  |
| Notification service | Provides alerts, schedules updates,  |
| System monitoring service | Logs system activity, catches errors and provides monitoring visibility to system maintainers |
| Conversational service | Core user interface routing queries between subsystems and handling user responses |
| AI model and API keys service | Manages and updates AI model/API connections for dynamic, modular response capabilities |
| System failure and backup services  | Handles system failures, backs up data and restores information to maintain continuity |
| Storage services | Provides storage for user specific data, university information and system configurations  |
| Data integration services | Synchronized and imports data from external institutional sources on schedule |

   

Architectural Layers:

## Presentation Layer

* Conversational Service  
* Notifications Service


Business Logic Layer

* User and User Permissions Service  
* User Authentication Service  
* System Monitoring Service  
* AI Model and API Keys Service​  
* System Failure and Backup Services


Data Layer

* Storage Services​  
* Data Integration Services

   This design improves modularity, makes responsibilities clear, and ensures testable interfaces, supporting many users and easy integration. The system is now scalable and secure, with a solid foundation for adding more features later
